title: Determination 45/1/226: glazing in the rear wall of a new office building near the boundary (Requirement B4; section 50(2))
jurisdiction: England (UK): Secretary of State determination / appeal / tribunal under the Building Act 1984 and Building Regulations; comparative test only, not Alberta
code_edition: Building Regulations 2000 (as amended): Requirement B4 (external fire spread)

facts.text: The proposed building is a new office building of basement, ground and four upper floors (six storeys in total); its rear wall is 215mm from the site boundary and has several large windows.
The approved inspector considered that the fire engineer's report did not adequately demonstrate compliance with Requirement B4 for the rear-wall glazing and rejected the proposals on that basis.
The fire engineer's modelling assumes standard 6mm double glazing keeps its integrity while the glazing stays below 600 C (the source text reads '600oC').
The approved inspector's case is that the glazing should give 60 minutes integrity and insulation given the boundary proximity; the applicant relies on computer modelling.
The Secretary of State's view is that to comply with Requirement B4 the external walls should be constructed so that the risk of ignition from an external source is controlled.
Determination: the plans do not comply with Requirement B4 (External Fire Spread) of Schedule 1 to the Building Regulations 2000 (as amended).
The determination is made under section 50(2) of the Building Act 1984 (approved inspectors), not section 16.
